records.text: I was arrested on September 3 in Congress for calling out AIPAC.
records.speaker: Anthony Aguilar

appearances.snippet: Candace Anthony Aguilar, the Gaza whistleblower, Green Beret, I've been to Gaza. I was arrested on the 3rd of September in Congress for calling out AIPAC. I'd love to come on and talk.

verification.notes: Aguilar was removed and arrested on September 3, 2025 after interrupting a Senate Foreign Relations Committee hearing. Video-based reports document that he and Josephine Guilbeau accused Congress of complicity in Gaza and protested U.S. support for Israel; the reviewed recording/reporting does not show him specifically naming AIPAC, so that motive is his later characterization rather than a fully confirmed description of the interruption.

sources.title: Army Veterans Disrupt Senate Hearing to Accuse Members of Complicity in Gaza Genocide
sources.relevance: Confirms Aguilar's September 3 removal/arrest and records the subject of his protest.

records.text: The administration did not voluntarily release the Epstein files; Congress forced the release with a veto-proof majority.
records.speaker: Jared Moskowitz

appearances.snippet: You guys didn't release the files. ... You were forced by Congress. ... Every member of the House except one and the entire Senate. ... The reason the president signed it is because it was a veto-proof majority. ... and yet the entire House but one member and the whole Senate forced the administration to release the files.

verification.notes: Congress's official action record shows the Epstein Files Transparency Act passed the House 427-1 and the Senate by unanimous consent, margins sufficient to override a veto. The White House records that President Trump signed H.R. 4405 into law.

sources.title: H.R. 4405 All Actions
sources.relevance: Official legislative history records the 427-1 House vote and Senate unanimous consent.

sources.title: H.R. 4405 Signed Into Law

records.text: Congressional officials hear the critical information and risk analysis we present about power-grid threats, but they do not want to take action
records.speaker: Erika Kirk

appearances.snippet: So the concern that we have is that we put out this critical information and when we go over this risk analysis, they hear what we're saying but they don't want to take action.

verification.notes: The documentary clip establishes that Erika Kirk made this accusation, but it identifies no congressional officials, presentation dates, records, or responses. Live research on 2026-08-24 found no independent evidence establishing what officials heard or their alleged unwillingness to act; the claim about intent cannot be tested from public sources.

records.text: Brian Mast wore the uniform of a foreign country in Congress and spoke as though slaughtering Palestinians, including civilians, was acceptable.
records.speaker: Ana Kasparian

appearances.snippet: Like you were the wrong like you were in the wrong because you realize that you have a sitting United States congressman wearing the uniform of a foreign foreign country in the halls of Congress talking about how it's OK to just slaughter an entire group of people, including women, children, elderly people.

verification.notes: Mast did wear an IDF uniform at the Capitol and made statements denying the innocence of Palestinian civilians and comparing them with Nazi civilians. The clause that he spoke as though slaughter was acceptable is an interpretive characterization rather than a directly testable quotation.

records.text: Kash Patel told Congress he could not disclose information about Thomas Matthew Crooks because of a trial, even though no trial existed because Crooks was dead.

appearances.snippet: And Patel was like, I can't disclose that information because there's a trial, except there isn't a trial. Crooks is dead. So, you know, like we want to learn more about his motives. Like, where is he from?

verification.notes: The official House hearing transcript shows Rep. Hunt asked Patel to answer previously submitted Thomas Crooks questions and Patel replied, As soon as the trial is over.
